evidence: Analytic Gamma log Levy exponent with nonnegative Levy measure; exact Mellin transform Gamma(1+s)^tau, s>-1.

correctness.rationale: For 0<p<1 set tau=1-p. The compensated Gamma Levy exponent makes log E, for E unit-exponential, infinitely divisible; its tau-power determines a real Y with E exp(sY)=Gamma(1+s)^tau for s>-1. Thus X=exp(Y)>0 has E X^n=(n!)^tau and all positive exponential moments, so E exp(zX)=F_p(z). Its E X^{-q}=Gamma(1-q)^tau diverges as q tends to 1 from below; restriction to X<=1 plus monotone convergence proves E X^{-1}=infinity. Tonelli gives integral_0^infty F_p(-x)dx=infinity while dominated convergence yields F_p(-x)->0. The coefficient order is 1/p finite. If F_p had finitely many zeros, Hadamard gives F_p=P exp(Q); positivity on the negative ray forces Q(-x) real modulo a constant phase. A nonconstant real polynomial Q(-x) either grows, contradicting F_p(-x)->0, or decays, contradicting nonintegrability; a constant Q makes F_p a polynomial, also impossible. Therefore infinitely many zeros, none on either real half-axis; conjugation yields infinitely many off-real pairs. The separate Rosas p>1 theorem and F_1=exp finish the positive-p classification.
risks: Uses classical Levy-Khintchine existence and finite-order Hadamard factorization as named external theorems; does not quantify zeros or locate them.

evidence: Sharp boundary p=1 is the unique zero-free positive exponent, p>1 previously known.
Strict complete monotonicity coexists with infinitely many nonreal zeros, an interpretable special-function phenomenon.
value.rationale: The exact infinite/nonreal zero classification fills a natural missing regime of the factorial-power entire-function family, including delicate reciprocal-integer parameters where an order-only argument is insufficient. Its reusable inverse-moment criterion is a motivated analytic mechanism, not a routine numerical root count.
risks: No zero-density or multiplicity description; significance is the zero classification and criterion, not those stronger unknowns.
